data.narrative:
Bright Machines, founded by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan, is a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $300M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—operating in the same sector and stage proximity, including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised ($300M) as a proxy for Series C entry value, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $510M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer cohort reflects both earlier-stage (Series B) and later-stage (Series D) benchmarks, accounting for stage dispersion within the robotics subsector.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $434M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median implied value of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate comparables and the heterogeneity of growth trajectories within frontier robotics. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the robustness of the 7-company dataset; however, stage progression provides a conservative floor. Key uncertainties include unit economics, deployment scale, and customer concentration—factors not directly reflected in the peer valuation multiples.
